agent_exec.description: The capstone composition layer that chains all safety mechanisms together into a single entry point for agent operations. Provides guard checks, contract validation, observability, atomic execution, retry/timeout, compensating transactions, and error recovery playbooks. Phase 5.4 of the MAINFRAME agent safety framework.

agent_undo_register.description: Register an undo action for the current operation chain Undo actions execute in LIFO order (last registered = first undone)

agent_undo_all.description: Execute all registered undo actions (rollback) in LIFO order

agent_undo_stack.description: Get undo stack as JSON array Output: [{"label":"...","command":"...","registered_at":N}]

agent_transaction.description: Execute a sequence of commands with automatic rollback on failure Each command has a paired undo command do: mkdir -p /tmp/project undo: rm -rf /tmp/project do: cp config.json /tmp/project/ undo: rm /tmp/project/config.json EOF

agent_recovery_register.description: Register a recovery strategy for an error pattern

agent_recover.description: Attempt automatic recovery from a failed command

agent_recovery_list.description: List registered recovery playbooks Output: pattern -> command pairs

agent_recovery_suggest.description: Get recovery suggestion without executing Output: JSON {"pattern":"matched","command":"fix_cmd","description":"what it does"}

agent_should_skip.description: Check if an operation should be skipped (idempotency check)

agent_observe.description: Run a command with full observability (timing, output capture) Output: JSON {"command":"...","exit_code":0,"duration_ms":N,"stdout_bytes":N,"stderr_bytes":N}

agent_context_start.description: Create a named execution context (groups related operations)

agent_pipeline.description: Run multiple commands in sequence with pipeline safety

agent_exec.description: The unified agent execution wrapper Chains: guard -> contract -> idempotent -> observe -> execute -> retry/timeout -> verify -> undo-on-fail

agent.description: File-based IPC for multi-agent coordination. Provides agent registration, discovery, messaging (point-to-point and broadcast), work queues, and synchronization primitives (barriers, signals).

agent_register.description: Register an agent with optional capabilities. Creates directory structure: agents/<name>/registered    (timestamp) agents/<name>/capabilities  (one per line) agents/<name>/heartbeat     (epoch) agents/<name>/inbox/        (incoming messages) agents/<name>/outbox/       (sent messages log)

agent_unregister.description: Unregister an agent, removing all state. If no name given, unregisters current agent.

agent_discover.description: Discover agents with a specific capability.

agent_list.description: List all registered agents with their capabilities as JSON.

agent_status.description: Get agent status as JSON object with registration time, heartbeat, capabilities, and message count.

agent_heartbeat.description: Update the heartbeat timestamp for the current agent.

agent_send.description: Send a message to a target agent. The message is written as a JSON file into the target agent's inbox directory.

agent_receive.description: Receive the next message from the agent's inbox (FIFO order). Uses flock for atomic consumption. Waits up to TIMEOUT seconds.

agent_broadcast.description: Broadcast a message to all registered agents.

agent_peek.description: View the next message in the inbox without removing it.

agent_inbox_count.description: Get the number of pending messages in the inbox.

agent_clear_inbox.description: Delete all pending messages from the inbox.

agent_work_queue.description: Create or ensure a named work queue exists.

agent_work_push.description: Push an item onto a work queue. Items are JSON payloads.

agent_work_pop.description: Pop the next item from a work queue (FIFO, atomic with flock).

agent_work_count.description: Count the number of items remaining in a work queue.

agent_work_clear.description: Remove all items from a work queue.

agent_barrier.description: Barrier synchronization: wait until COUNT agents reach the same barrier. Each agent calls agent_barrier with the same NAME. When COUNT agents have called it, all are released.

agent_signal.description: Signal a named event. Any agents waiting via agent_wait will be released.

agent_wait.description: Wait for a named signal event.

agent_info.description: Get detailed info for an agent (alias for agent_status).

agent_info_v.description: Store agent info in a variable (nameref variant).

agent_prune.description: Remove agents that haven't sent a heartbeat within the specified time.

agent_list_v.description: Store list of agent names in an array (nameref variant).

agent_receive_async.description: Non-blocking receive: returns immediately if no message available.

agent_subscribe.description: Subscribe an agent to a topic for pub/sub messaging.

agent_unsubscribe.description: Unsubscribe an agent from a topic.

agent_publish.description: Publish a message to all subscribers of a topic.

agent_lock.description: Acquire an exclusive lock on a named resource. This is a blocking operation that waits until the lock is available.

agent_trylock.description: Try to acquire a lock without blocking.

agent_work_push_tracked.description: Push an item onto a work queue and return its task ID. This is an enhanced version that returns a trackable ID.

agent_work_fail.description: Mark a task as failed with a reason.

agent_work_stats.description: Get statistics for a work queue.

agent_work_pop_tracked.description: Enhanced work_pop that tracks in-progress status

agent_find_by_capability.description: Find agents by capability (alias for agent_discover).

agent_elect_leader.description: Simple leader election among registered agents. Uses lexicographic ordering for determinism.

agent_cleanup.description: Clean up all agent resources (for testing/shutdown).

agent_init.description: Initialize the agent subsystem (creates base directories).

ansi.description: Terminal formatting with ANSI escape sequences

ansi_erase_down.description: Erase from cursor to end of screen

ansi_erase_up.description: Erase from cursor to beginning of screen

ansi_erase_line_end.description: Erase from cursor to end of line

ansi_erase_line_start.description: Erase from cursor to beginning of line

ansi_clear.description: Clear screen and move to home

args_usage_string.description: Generate usage string (for USAGE variable used by die_usage)

async.description: Async operations, timers, and job management for bash

async_kill.description: Kill a specific job by PID

set_timeout.description: Execute command after delay (like JavaScript setTimeout)

set_interval.description: Execute command repeatedly at interval (like JavaScript setInterval)

async_callback.description: Execute command and call callback with result

parallel_limit.description: Execute commands in parallel with a limit

parallel_map.description: Map function over array in parallel

coproc_start.description: Start a coprocess for bidirectional communication Note: Use ${COPROC[0]} to read, ${COPROC[1]} to write

retry_callback.description: Retry with callback on each failure

atomic.description: File write operations that prevent partial state through temp-file-then-rename patterns, flock for concurrent access, and checkpoint/rollback mechanisms for safe recovery.

atomic_write.description: Write content to a file atomically. Writes to a temporary file first, then renames it to the target. The rename is atomic on POSIX filesystems, preventing any reader from seeing partial content.

atomic_append.description: Append content to a file with file locking for concurrent safety. Uses flock to prevent interleaved writes from multiple processes.

atomic_replace.description: Replace file content with automatic backup for rollback. Creates a timestamped backup, writes new content atomically, and verifies the write succeeded before completing.

safe_remove.description: Move file/directory to trash instead of permanent deletion. Files can be recovered with safe_restore.

safe_restore.description: Restore the most recently trashed file with the given name.

file_checkpoint.description: Create a named checkpoint (snapshot) of a file for later rollback. Multiple checkpoints can coexist with different names.

file_rollback.description: Restore a file from a named checkpoint.

file_checkpoints.description: List all checkpoints, optionally filtered by file path.

file_checkpoint_cleanup.description: Clean up checkpoints older than N seconds (default: 86400 = 24h).

cache.description: Function memoization with TTL, content-addressable store, session cache, dependency-aware invalidation, LRU eviction, and concurrency-safe operations for AI agent workflows.

memoize.description: Memoize a function call with optional TTL and file-dependency invalidation. On cache hit: outputs cached value, returns 0. On cache miss: runs function, caches output, returns function's exit code.

memoize_clear.description: Clear memoized cache entries, optionally matching a pattern. Without pattern, clears all memoized entries.

memoize_stats.description: Display memoization statistics: hit/miss counts, hit ratio.

cas_store.description: Store content by its SHA-256 hash. Returns the hash on stdout. Duplicate content is automatically deduplicated.

cas_get.description: Retrieve content from the CAS by its hash.

cas_exists.description: Check if content exists in the CAS.

cas_gc.description: Garbage collect old CAS entries based on modification time.

session_cache_set.description: Store a value in the in-memory session cache. Session cache persists only for the lifetime of the current shell.

session_cache_get.description: Retrieve a value from the in-memory session cache.

session_cache_clear.description: Clear the entire in-memory session cache.

session_cache_has.description: Check if a key exists in the session cache.

session_cache_stats.description: Display session cache statistics: entry count, estimated memory usage.

cache_invalidate.description: Invalidate cache entries matching a pattern. Supports: exact cache key, function name prefix, or shell glob.

cache_clear.description: Clear the entire cache (memo + CAS + locks).

cache_stats.description: Display cache statistics: hit/miss ratio, size, entry count.

cache_max_size.description: Set the maximum cache size. Triggers eviction if current size exceeds new limit.

cache_evict_lru.description: Evict least-recently-used cache entries to stay within size limits. Uses file modification time as LRU proxy.

cache_depends_on.description: Register file dependencies for a cache key. When files change (hash differs), the cache entry is considered stale.

cache_check_deps.description: Check if file dependencies for a cache key have changed. Compares current file hashes against stored dependency hashes.
examples: if cache_check_deps "$key"; then echo "still valid"; fi

cache_warm.description: Warm the cache by preloading common operations for a project type. Useful for speeding up first-time operations in a new session.

config_load.description: Find and load the first available configuration file

config_require.description: Require a configuration value to be set

confirm.description: Interactive and automated confirmation gates for AI agent operations. Supports policy-based auto-approve/deny, risk-based decisions (integrates with risk.sh), timeout-based denials, batch confirmations, and full audit history as JSON.

mainframe_confirm.description: Interactive yes/no confirmation prompt. Respects _MAINFRAME_CONFIRM_MODE for auto-approve/deny in CI/testing environments.
mainframe_confirm.signature: if mainframe_confirm "Deploy to production?"; then deploy; fi

mainframe_confirm_risk.description: Auto-approve if the command's risk score is below the threshold. If mainframe_risk_score is available (from risk.sh), uses it for scoring. Falls back to always-ask if risk.sh is not loaded.

mainframe_confirm_batch.description: Show a batch of commands and confirm all-or-nothing. User sees the full list before making a single decision.

mainframe_confirm_timeout.description: Confirmation with a timeout. If the user does not respond within the specified number of seconds, the request is automatically denied.

mainframe_confirm_policy.description: Set the confirmation policy for subsequent operations. always - always prompt for confirmation never  - auto-approve everything (dangerous for production) risk   - use risk scoring to decide (requires risk.sh)

mainframe_confirm_threshold.description: Set the risk threshold for auto-approve in risk-based policy mode. Commands with risk scores below this threshold are auto-approved. Commands at or above this threshold require interactive confirmation.

mainframe_confirm_log.description: Show the full confirmation history as a JSON array. Each entry contains timestamp, message, decision, and method.

mainframe_confirm_count.description: Return the number of entries in the confirmation history.

mainframe_confirm_last.description: Show the most recent confirmation decision.

mainframe_confirm_auto_approve.description: Force auto-approve mode. All confirmations return 0 without prompting. Useful for CI/testing environments where interactive input is unavailable.

mainframe_confirm_auto_deny.description: Force auto-deny mode. All confirmations return 1 without prompting. Useful for CI/testing environments to verify denial paths.

mainframe_confirm_reset.description: Reset to interactive mode. Confirmations will prompt via /dev/tty. Also resets policy to "always" and threshold to 5.

mainframe_confirm_status.description: Show current confirmation module status including mode, policy, threshold, and history count.

context.description: Helps AI agents estimate token costs, manage context budgets, and truncate/summarize content to fit within model limits.

context_estimate_tokens.description: Estimate token count for a string Uses character-based heuristic (~4 chars/token for English, ~3.5 for code) Output: integer token count (approximate)

context_file_tokens.description: Estimate tokens for a file Output: integer token count (approximate)

context_command_tokens.description: Estimate tokens for command output (runs command, counts result) Output: integer token count Side effect: stores command output in $_CTX_LAST_OUTPUT for reuse

context_ratio.description: Get character-to-token ratio for a content type Output: float ratio (e.g., "3.5")

context_budget_init.description: Initialize a context budget shellcheck disable=SC2120  # function has optional args with defaults

context_budget_use.description: Record token usage with a label

context_budget_remaining.description: Check remaining budget Output: integer remaining tokens (max - used - reserve)

context_budget_fits.description: Check if a token count fits within the remaining budget

context_budget_summary.description: Get budget summary as JSON Output: JSON object with budget details

context_truncate.description: Truncate text to fit within N tokens Strategies: head   - keep first N tokens (default) tail   - keep last N tokens middle - keep start and end, cut middle smart  - keep first paragraph + last paragraph + truncation marker

context_truncate_file.description: Truncate a file's content to fit within max_tokens

context_distribute_budget.description: Distribute token budget across multiple items by priority Reads JSON-like input from stdin: label\tcontent\tpriority (tab-separated) Output: JSON with truncated content per item

context_analyze.description: Analyze content complexity (affects token estimation accuracy) Output: JSON with chars, lines, estimated_tokens, type, language, density

context_detect_type.description: Detect content type and language Output: "code:python" or "code:bash" or "text:prose" or "data:json" etc.

context_chunk_size.description: Get optimal chunk size for content type and model Output: recommended max tokens per chunk

context_batch_files.description: Determine which files from stdin fit within a token budget Output: file paths that fit, one per line

context_read_plan.description: Plan file reading order to maximize coverage within budget Output: JSON plan with file details and inclusion status

contract.description: Precondition/postcondition assertions, type checking, and structured JSON error reporting that AI agents can parse for automated debugging and recovery.

mainframe_error.description: Emit a structured error with code, message, calling function, file, and line. AI agents parse this JSON to understand failures and take corrective action.

contract_require.description: Assert a precondition. If it fails, emit structured error and return 1. Use at the top of functions to validate inputs.

contract_ensure.description: Assert a postcondition. If it fails, emit structured error. Use before returning from functions to validate outputs.

contract_invariant.description: Assert an invariant that should always hold. Emits structured error on failure.

contract_type_check.description: Check if a value matches an expected type. Supported types: int, float, string, bool, file, dir, path, nonempty

contract_not_empty.description: Assert that all provided arguments are non-empty strings. Common precondition for functions requiring arguments.

contract_is_file.description: Assert that a file exists. Emits structured error with path context.

contract_is_dir.description: Assert that a directory exists. Emits structured error with path context.

contract_in_range.description: Assert that an integer value is within a given range [min, max].

contracts_disable.description: Disable contract checking globally (for production performance).

constant_time_compare.description: Compare two strings in constant time (mitigate timing attacks) Note: Bash has inherent timing variations; this is best-effort

csv_parse_multiline.description: Parse multiline CSV content (handles newlines in quoted fields)

csv_has_header.description: Check if first row looks like a header

device_list_usb.description: device_list_usb List USB/removable drives only (RM=1 or TRAN=usb)

device_list_unmounted.description: device_list_unmounted List partitions with no mountpoint

device_list_mounted.description: device_list_mounted List currently mounted filesystems (from findmnt)

device_fstype.description: device_fstype DEVICE Get filesystem type for device

device_is_removable.description: device_is_removable DEVICE Return 0 if removable, 1 if not

device_uuid.description: device_uuid DEVICE Get UUID for device (Linux only, requires blkid)

device_mount.description: device_mount DEVICE DIRECTORY Mount device to directory. Requires sudo.

device_eject.description: device_eject DEVICE Unmount + power-off for safe USB removal. Verifies removable first.

device_find_by_uuid.description: device_find_by_uuid UUID Find device path by UUID

device_find_by_fstype.description: device_find_by_fstype FSTYPE Find devices by filesystem type. Output: device paths, one per line.

device_summary_oneliner.description: device_summary_oneliner Quick summary: "3 disks | 2 USB | 1.2TB free"

diff.description: Surgical file editing for AI agents via unified diffs, search-and-replace, and safe patch application. Enables agents to make precise edits without dumping/rewriting entire files.

diff_strings.description: Generate unified diff between two strings. Uses temp files internally, cleans up after.

diff_files.description: Generate unified diff between two files.

diff_preview.description: Generate diff between a file and new content (preview changes).

diff_edit_script.description: Generate a minimal line-based edit script. Output format: "dN" (delete line N), "aN:text" (add after N), "cN:text" (change N)

diff_apply.description: Apply a unified diff to a file. Creates backup by default.

diff_apply_string.description: Apply a unified diff to a string (pure in-memory).

diff_reverse.description: Reverse-apply a diff (undo a patch). Swaps + and - lines in the diff then applies.

diff_replace.description: Replace exact text in a file. Primary editing primitive for AI agents. Handles multiline text. Atomic write with optional backup.

diff_replace_string.description: Replace text in a string. Handles multiline.

diff_insert_after.description: Insert text after a matching line in a file.

diff_insert_before.description: Insert text before a matching line in a file.

diff_delete_lines.description: Delete lines matching a pattern from a file.

diff_replace_range.description: Replace a range of lines in a file (1-based line numbers).

diff_can_apply.description: Check if a diff can be cleanly applied.

diff_conflicts.description: Show what conflicts would occur if diff were applied.

diff_validate_unique.description: Validate that old_text exists exactly once in file.

diff_stats.description: Count changes in a unified diff.

diff_changed_lines.description: Extract just the changed lines from a diff.

diff_affected_lines.description: Get the line numbers affected by a diff (in the original file).

docker_running.description: Check if Docker daemon is running

Integrates with USOP (output.sh) for structured output and risk.sh for automatic risk scoring of planned operations.

mainframe_dryrun_enabled.description: Check whether dry-run mode is currently enabled.

mainframe_plan_add.description: Record a planned operation. In dry-run mode, records but does not execute. In normal mode, executes immediately and records for audit trail.

mainframe_plan_show.description: Display the current plan in the specified format.

mainframe_plan_clear.description: Clear all recorded plan steps and reset the counter.

mainframe_plan_count.description: Print the number of currently recorded plan steps.

mainframe_plan_execute.description: Execute the recorded plan. With --confirm, displays the plan and waits for user confirmation before proceeding. With --step N, executes only that step. With --continue-on-error, does not abort on first failure.

mainframe_plan_export.description: Export the plan to a file or stdout. Uses MAINFRAME_PLAN_FORMAT for formatting.

mainframe_plan_remove.description: Remove a specific step from the plan by its step number.

mainframe_plan_reorder.description: Move a step from one position to another, shifting other steps accordingly.

mainframe_plan_risk_summary.description: Show aggregate risk information: total score, max score, and distribution across risk levels. Useful for approval gates.

mainframe_plan_results.description: Display the success/failure status of each executed step.

catch.description: End try block and check for errors - returns 0 if error occurred (for catch)

errors.description: Comprehensive error code constants with human-readable messages and actionable recovery suggestions for AI coding assistants. Maps common failure scenarios to structured codes that agents can use for automated debugging and self-correction.

mainframe_error_msg.description: Get the human-readable message for an error code.

mainframe_error_suggest.description: Get the recovery suggestion for an error code. Suggestions are actionable - they tell the AI agent exactly what to call.

mainframe_error_category.description: Get the category for an error code based on its numeric range.

mainframe_error_list.description: List all error codes, optionally filtered by category. Output format: CODE  NAME  MESSAGE
examples: mainframe_error_list path | while read -r code name msg; do ...; done

is_not_empty.description: Check if string is not empty

fp_map_v.description: Map with nameref output (no subshells) Note: The function must accept 2 args: value and output variable name For simple functions, use fp_map_v_simple instead

fp_map_v_nr.description: Map with nameref output using nameref-aware functions The function signature: func(value, result_varname)

fp_reduce.description: Reduce elements to single value (stdout version)

fp_reduce_v_nr.description: Reduce with nameref-aware binary function (fully subshell-free) The function signature: func(acc, value, result_varname)

fp_find.description: Find first element matching predicate Returns 1 if not found

fp_find_v.description: Find with nameref output (no subshell) Returns 0 if found, 1 if not found

fp_find_index.description: Find index of first matching element Returns 1 if not found

fp_any.description: Check if any element matches predicate

fp_all.description: Check if all elements match predicate

fp_none.description: Check if no elements match predicate

fp_compose.description: Compose functions (right to left) eval "$composed 5"  # double(5)=10, then increment(10)=11

fp_pipe.description: Pipe functions (left to right) eval "$piped 5"  # double(5)=10, then increment(10)=11

fp_partition_v.description: Partition elements into two arrays by predicate

fp_zip.description: Zip two arrays together Output: element pairs on separate lines (tab-separated)

fp_group_by.description: Group by function result Note: Outputs key<tab>value pairs

fzf_available.description: Return 0 if fzf is installed, 1 if not

fzf_select.description: Read stdin lines, present interactive menu, output selection on stdout Options: --multi, --prompt "text", --header "text", --preview "cmd {}", --height N

fzf_file.description: Select a file from a directory (default: current dir)

fzf_git_branch.description: Select a git branch, output clean branch name

fzf_git_log.description: Select a git commit, output commit hash

fzf_git_file.description: Select a tracked git file, output file path

fzf_docker_container.description: Select a docker container, output container ID

fzf_port.description: Select a listening port, output port number

fzf_env.description: Select an environment variable, output VAR=value

fzf_history.description: Select from shell history, output the command

git_is_repo.description: Check if current directory is a git repository

git_branches.description: List all local branches (one per line)

git_is_dirty.description: Check if working tree has uncommitted changes

git_is_clean.description: Check if working tree is clean (no uncommitted changes)

git_has_staged.description: Check if there are staged changes

git_has_unstaged.description: Check if there are unstaged changes

git_has_untracked.description: Check if there are untracked files

git_commits_ahead.description: Get commits ahead of remote tracking branch

git_commits_behind.description: Get commits behind remote tracking branch

git_is_pushed.description: Check if current branch is pushed to remote

git_ignore_check.description: Check if a file is gitignored

git_file_history.description: Get commit history for a specific file

git_blame_line.description: Get blame info for a specific line

git_diff_files.description: List files changed between two refs

git_diff_stat.description: Get diff statistics between two refs

git_merge_base.description: Find common ancestor of two branches

git_log_oneline.description: Get last N commits, one line each

git_changed_since.description: List files changed since a ref

git_has_stash.description: Check if there are stashed changes

git_config_exists.description: Check if a config key is set

go.description: Static analysis of Go projects using pure bash. Extracts imports, builds dependency graphs, detects circular dependencies, and provides project health metrics without requiring the Go toolchain.

go_is_project.description: go_is_project DIR Check if directory is a Go project (has go.mod)

go_source_dir.description: go_source_dir DIR Determine the main source directory

go_file_imports.description: go_file_imports FILE Extract import paths from a Go file (handles single and grouped imports) Output: one import path per line

go_import_frequency.description: go_import_frequency DIR List most-used packages across the project Output: "COUNT PACKAGE" sorted by frequency

go_import_graph.description: go_import_graph DIR Build file-to-imports mapping Output: "file:import1,import2,..."

go_circular_deps.description: go_circular_deps DIR Detect circular dependencies between packages Output: "pkg_a <-> pkg_b" for each cycle found

go_module_info.description: go_module_info DIR Parse go.mod for module name and Go version Output: "module=NAME,go_version=VERSION,require_count=N"

go_dep_count.description: go_dep_count DIR Count direct and indirect dependencies Output: "direct=N,indirect=N"

go_function_count.description: go_function_count DIR Count function definitions (including methods)

go_loc.description: go_loc DIR Count lines of code (excluding blank lines, // comments, and /* */ blocks)

go_test_coverage.description: go_test_coverage DIR Count test files and test functions Output: "test_files=N,test_functions=N"

go_summary.description: go_summary DIR Generate JSON project health overview NOTE: Each metric function independently calls _go_find_files. For large projects, consider caching the file list externally and using xargs.

guard.description: Pre-execution guards and runtime checks for common failure modes targeting AI coding assistant error prevention.

guard_init.description: Initialize all guards - call at script start Sets: -euo pipefail, error handlers, cleanup traps

guard_path_safe.description: Guard: Path must be safe (no traversal outside base)

guard_var_set.description: Guard: Variable must be set (and optionally non-empty) shellcheck disable=SC2163  # Dynamic export is intentional

guard_var_safe.description: Guard: Variable is safe for shell use (no injection characters)

guard_commands.description: Guard: All required commands must exist

guard_file_op.description: Guard: File operation safety (combines multiple checks)

hints.description: Suggests what function to call next based on workflow patterns. Provides contextual hints for AI coding assistants and developers to discover optimal function chains across MAINFRAME libraries.

mainframe_hint.description: Get hint for a function (returns suggested next functions) Output: format_bytes,file_lines,read_file

mainframe_hints_for.description: List all hints in a category Output: git_branch -> git_commit_hash,git_is_dirty,git_log_oneline git_is_dirty -> git_changed_files,git_status_short,git_has_staged ...

mainframe_hints_chain.description: Show chain of hints starting from a function Output: git_branch -> git_commit_hash -> git_commit_message -> trim_string git_branch -> git_commit_hash -> git_commit_author -> git_commit_date git_branch -> git_commit_hash -> git_log_oneline -> git_changed_since git_branch -> git_is_dirty -> git_changed_files -> array_length ...

mainframe_hint_category.description: Get the category a function belongs to Output: git

mainframe_hints_count.description: Count total number of hints in the database

http.description: HTTP client using /dev/tcp for pure bash network operations

url_encode.description: URL encode a string Note: If urlencode from pure-string.sh exists, this aliases to it

url_parse.description: Parse URL into components Sets: URL_SCHEME, URL_HOST, URL_PORT, URL_PATH, URL_QUERY, URL_USER, URL_PASS

query_string.description: Build query string from key=value pairs

http_header.description: Format a single HTTP header line

http_request.description: Low-level HTTP request builder and sender

http_status.description: Extract HTTP status code from response

http_header_get.description: Get specific header value from response

http_headers.description: Get all headers as newline-separated list

http_json_post.description: POST JSON data with appropriate Content-Type

http_is_success.description: Check if HTTP status indicates success (2xx)

http_is_redirect.description: Check if HTTP status indicates redirect (3xx)

http_is_client_error.description: Check if HTTP status indicates client error (4xx)

http_is_server_error.description: Check if HTTP status indicates server error (5xx)

idempotent.description: Check-before-act operations that produce the same result regardless of how many times they're executed. Essential for AI coding assistants that frequently re-run scripts after context loss or retry failed operations.

ensure_dir.description: Create directory only if it doesn't exist. Optionally set permissions if provided.

ensure_file.description: Create file with content only if it doesn't exist or content differs. If content is not provided, creates empty file (like touch).

ensure_line.description: Append a line to a file only if it's not already present. Uses a marker for identification if the line might appear as substring.

ensure_symlink.description: Create or fix symlink to point to the correct target. If link exists but points elsewhere, it's replaced. If something else exists at link path, fails unless force=true.

ensure_mount.description: Mount a device at a mountpoint only if not already mounted. Creates the mountpoint directory if needed.

ensure_service.description: Start a system service only if it's not already running. Supports systemd, init.d, and simple process checks.

ensure_package.description: Install a package only if it's not already installed. Auto-detects package manager (apt, dnf, yum, pacman, brew, apk).

ensure_dirs.description: Ensure multiple directories exist in one call.

ensure_lines.description: Ensure multiple lines exist in a file.

ensure_command.description: Verify a command is available (doesn't install, just checks). Use ensure_package for install behavior.

file_write_if_changed.description: Write file only if content differs (avoids unnecessary mtime changes, CI rebuilds). Uses atomic write (temp + rename) to prevent partial writes on failure.

file_write_if_changed_nl.description: Write file with trailing newline only if content differs. Convenience wrapper for POSIX-compliant text files.

file_append_if_missing.description: Append to file only if the line doesn't already exist. Uses fixed-string exact-line matching (grep -Fx).

file_write_json_if_changed.description: Write JSON file only if parsed content differs (ignores formatting). When jq is available, normalizes both sides (sorted keys, compact) before comparison. Falls back to byte comparison when jq is not installed.

json_value.description: Auto-detect type and create appropriate JSON value

json_array_typed.description: Create JSON array with explicit types

json_array_from_lines.description: Create JSON array from newline-separated string

json_object.description: Create JSON object from key=value pairs

json_from_assoc.description: Create JSON object from associative array

json_merge.description: Merge multiple JSON objects (simple, top-level only)

json_get.description: Extract string value by key (simple, top-level only)

json_escape_v.description: Escape string for JSON into variable

json_array_v.description: Create JSON array from arguments into variable

json_array_typed_v.description: Create JSON array with explicit types into variable

json_object_v.description: Create JSON object from key=value pairs into variable

json_from_assoc_v.description: Create JSON object from associative array into variable

json_get_v.description: Extract value by key into variable (simple, top-level only)

json_merge_v.description: Merge multiple JSON objects into variable (simple, top-level only)

limits.description: Resource limit tracking and enforcement for AI agent operations. Provides configurable caps on file operations, write volume, execution time, recursion depth, and network operations. Prevents runaway agents from consuming unbounded resources.

mainframe_limit_init.description: Initialize the limits tracking system. Creates a temporary directory for counter files and marks the system as active.

mainframe_limit_files.description: Set the maximum number of file operations (open, read, write, delete) allowed.

mainframe_limit_writes.description: Set the maximum total write volume allowed. Accepts human-readable sizes.

mainframe_limit_time.description: Set the maximum execution time in seconds.

mainframe_limit_depth.description: Set the maximum recursion or nesting depth.

mainframe_limit_network.description: Set the maximum number of network operations allowed.

mainframe_limit_check.description: Check whether a specific limit has been exceeded. For time limits, calculates elapsed time since init.

mainframe_limit_increment.description: Increment a usage counter. Used to track resource consumption.

mainframe_limit_status.description: Display status of all limits with current usage and maximums.

mainframe_limit_reset.description: Reset usage counters. With no argument, resets all counters. With a type argument, resets only that counter.

mainframe_limit_remaining.description: Show the remaining quota for a specific limit type. Prints "unlimited" if no limit is set (max=0).

mainframe_limit_enforce.description: Run a command only if the current limits allow it. Checks all active limits (those with max > 0) before executing. Increments the files counter by 1 after successful execution.

mainframe_limit_is_enabled.description: Check if the limits system is currently active.

meta.description: Variable introspection, dynamic calls, namerefs, constants

var_get.description: Get variable value by name (indirect expansion)
var_get.signature: var_get "varname" result_var  (no subshell, stores in result_var)

var_exists.description: Check if variable is set (may be empty)

var_nonempty.description: Check if variable is set and non-empty

vars_with_prefix.description: Get all variable names matching prefix Populates result_array with matching variable names

vars_matching.description: Get all variable names matching pattern (glob)

var_is_assoc.description: Check if variable is associative array

const_default.description: Define constant if not already set

func_source.description: Get function source file and line (if available)

var_ref.description: Create a nameref to a variable Note: Creates local nameref; useful in functions

method_exists.description: Check if method exists for prefix

call_or_default.description: Call function if exists, otherwise return default

netscan.description: Pure-bash network utilities for port checking, host discovery, banner grabbing, and HTTP header extraction. Designed for defensive administration and AI-automated infrastructure checks.

port_check.description: Check if a TCP port is open on a host. Uses /dev/tcp first, falls back to nc/ncat if available.

host_alive.description: Check if a host is alive using ping (ICMP) or TCP fallback.

banner_grab.description: Grab the service banner from an open port. Connects and reads the first response line (useful for SSH, SMTP, FTP, etc.).

http_headers.description: Extract HTTP response headers from a URL. Uses curl if available, falls back to /dev/tcp for HTTP (not HTTPS).

monitor_port.description: Check port state and return structured JSON result. Useful for watchdog scripts and monitoring loops.

scan_range.description: Scan a host for open ports from a list or range. Returns JSON array of results.

parse_nmap.description: Parse nmap greppable output (-oG) into structured JSON. Each host becomes a JSON object with IP, hostname, and open ports.

observe.description: Trace, timing, and structured error reporting that produces JSON output AI coding assistants can parse for debugging, error recovery, and performance analysis.

trace_start.description: Begin a named trace. Returns a trace ID that must be passed to trace_step and trace_end. Captures start timestamp. State is stored in files to survive subshell boundaries.

trace_step.description: Record a step within an active trace. Each step has a name, optional status, and optional detail message.

trace_end.description: End a trace and emit a complete JSON summary including all steps, duration, and final status.

observe_command.description: Execute a command and capture its stdout, stderr, exit code, and duration as a structured JSON object. Useful for AI agents to understand command outcomes without parsing unstructured output.

stack_trace.description: Capture the current bash call stack as a JSON array. Each frame includes function name, source file, and line number. Useful for error reporting that AI agents can parse.

observe_error.description: Emit a structured error with code, message, function context, and stack. Designed for AI agents to parse and take corrective action.

observe_time.description: Get current timestamp suitable for duration calculations. Uses EPOCHREALTIME (bash 5.0+) or date fallback.

observe_elapsed.description: Calculate elapsed time between a start timestamp and now.

output.description: Enables all MAINFRAME functions to output structured JSON envelopes instead of raw text, making the toolkit machine-readable for AI coding agents. Provides mode detection, envelope functions, timing helpers, and the output_wrap meta-wrapper.

output_init.description: Initialize output system Sets default mode if not already set via environment

output_mode.description: Get or set output mode Without args: returns current mode With arg: sets mode if valid, returns 1 if invalid

output_is_json.description: Check if JSON output mode is active Returns 0 if MAINFRAME_OUTPUT=json

output_is_raw.description: Check if raw output mode is active Returns 0 if MAINFRAME_OUTPUT=raw or unset

output_is_minimal.description: Check if minimal output mode is active Returns 0 if MAINFRAME_OUTPUT=minimal

output_is_debug.description: Check if debug output mode is active Returns 0 if MAINFRAME_OUTPUT=debug

output_format.description: Returns the current output format (backward compat alias)

output_timer_elapsed.description: Get elapsed time since timer_start in milliseconds Returns 0 if timer was not started

output_success.description: Emit a success envelope Format depends on MAINFRAME_OUTPUT mode: raw:     plain data json:    {"ok":true,"data":"...","meta":{...},"hint":"..."} minimal: {"ok":true,"data":"..."} debug:   json + timestamp + caller

output_error.description: Emit an error envelope Format depends on MAINFRAME_OUTPUT mode: raw:     plain message to stderr json:    {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"...","msg":"...","suggestion":"..."}} minimal: {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"...","msg":"..."}} debug:   json + timestamp + caller

output_raw.description: Emit raw text regardless of output mode Always bypasses envelope formatting

output_json.description: Emit JSON string unchanged regardless of output mode Useful for custom JSON that shouldn't be wrapped

output_json_object.description: Emit JSON object data (already formatted JSON)

output_json_array.description: Emit JSON array data (already formatted JSON)

output_wrap.description: Wrap any function call with automatic USOP envelope Captures stdout, exit code, and timing

output_with_mode.description: Execute command with temporary output mode Restores original mode after execution

output_success_legacy.description: Legacy output_success (old format) Kept for backward compatibility with existing code

output_json_string_kv.description: Emit a JSON key-value pair with string value Output: "key":"value"

output_json_number.description: Emit a JSON key-value pair with number value Output: "key":42

output_json_bool.description: Emit a JSON key-value pair with boolean value Output: "key":true

output_json_null.description: Emit a JSON key-value pair with null value Output: "key":null

output_json_array_from_lines.description: Read stdin lines and output a JSON array of strings Output: ["line1","line2"]

output_list.description: Emit a list/array envelope (legacy format) Output: {"status":"success","data":["item1","item2","item3"],"count":3}

output_object.description: Emit a key-value object envelope (legacy format)

output_progress.description: Emit a progress envelope for streaming/long operations

mainframe_call.description: Invoke any MAINFRAME function with automatic USOP wrapping Captures stdout, stderr, exit code, and wraps in JSON envelope

output_auto.description: Auto-detect output mode and emit appropriate format (legacy)

output_structured_error.description: Create a rich error object with context for AI agent consumption

output_try.description: Wrap a command and produce structured error on failure

parse_output.description: Structured JSON parsing of common tool outputs. Eliminates per-agent regex hacking of compiler and test runner output.

parse_detect_format.description: Detect what kind of output this is Reads stdin, outputs format name

parse_output.description: Parse output with format auto-detection or explicit format

parse_failures_only.description: Extract just the failures/errors from parsed output Reads parse_output JSON from stdin, outputs only failures array

parse_error_count.description: Count total errors across parsed output Reads stdin, outputs integer

parse_is_success.description: Check if output indicates success (0 failures) Reads stdin, returns 0 if no failures

parse_summary.description: Format parsed output as human-readable summary Reads parsed JSON from stdin, outputs 1-2 line summary

parse_locations.description: Extract file:line references from parsed output (for editor integration) Reads stdin, outputs "file:line" pairs (one per line)

parsers.description: Pure-bash parsers for common formats: CSV, key-value configs, INI files, URLs, and semantic versions. All output JSON for AI agent consumption.

parse_csv_line.description: Parse a single CSV line into the global array PARSE_CSV_FIELDS. Handles quoted fields with commas and escaped quotes. Uses a global array to avoid subshell overhead.

parse_csv_json.description: Parse a CSV line and return as JSON array.

parse_key_value.description: Parse key-value pairs from input. Supports = and : separators, strips whitespace, ignores comments (# and ;) and blank lines.

parse_ini.description: Parse an INI file into nested JSON. Sections become top-level keys, with key-value pairs as nested objects.

parse_url.description: Parse a URL into its components: scheme, user, password, host, port, path, query, fragment. Returns a JSON object.

parse_semver.description: Parse a semantic version string into its components. Supports: major.minor.patch[-prerelease][+build]

semver_compare.description: Compare two semantic versions. Returns: -1 if v1 < v2 0 if v1 == v2 1 if v1 > v2

path.description: Cross-platform path operations without external tools

path_normalize.description: Normalize path by resolving . and .. and collapsing multiple slashes

path_absolute.description: Get absolute path (resolves to real filesystem path)

path_relative.description: Get relative path from base to target

path_to_unix.description: Convert Windows path to Unix path

path_to_windows.description: Convert Unix path to Windows path

path_quote.description: Quote path for safe shell usage

path_is_safe.description: Check if path is safe (no directory traversal outside base)

path_ensure_dir.description: Ensure parent directory exists (create if needed) Creates: /foo/bar/baz/

path_common_prefix.description: Find common prefix of multiple paths

path_has_parent_ref.description: Check if path contains parent reference (..)

path_is_hidden.description: Check if path is hidden (starts with .)

path_equals.description: Check if two paths are equivalent (after normalization)

path_split.description: Split path into array of components

path_resolve.description: Resolve symlinks to get real path

perf.description: Bash version detection, feature gating for modern Bash (5.0+/5.3+), and performance measurement utilities. Enables conditional use of fast-path features (namerefs, EPOCHREALTIME, current-shell subst) while maintaining Bash 4.0+ compatibility.

bash_version.description: Get the current Bash version as a dot-separated string.

bash_version_major.description: Get just the major version number.

bash_version_at_least.description: Check if the current Bash version is at least the specified version.

bash_has_feature.description: Check if a specific Bash feature is available. Features: - namerefs: declare -n (Bash 4.3+) - mapfile: mapfile/readarray builtin (Bash 4.0+) - associative_arrays: declare -A (Bash 4.0+) - epochrealtime: $EPOCHREALTIME variable (Bash 5.0+) - epochseconds: $EPOCHSECONDS variable (Bash 5.0+) - wait_n: wait -n for any child (Bash 4.3+) - lastpipe: shopt -s lastpipe (Bash 4.2+) - globasciiranges: shopt -s globasciiranges (Bash 4.3+) - inherit_errexit: shopt -s inherit_errexit (Bash 4.4+) - extglob: extended globbing (Bash 4.0+)

bash_features.description: List all known features and whether they're available. Returns a JSON object for AI agent consumption.

perf_timer_start.description: Start a named performance timer. Uses variable storage to avoid subshells. The timer value is stored in a global variable PERF_TIMER_<name>.

perf_timer_elapsed.description: Stop a named timer and print the elapsed duration in seconds.

perf_timer_stop.description: Stop a named timer and emit a JSON timing result.

perf_compare.description: Compare execution time of two commands/approaches. Runs each command N iterations and reports average times.

perf_setvar.description: Set a variable by name without subshell. Uses printf -v which is significantly faster than var=$(command) for simple assignments. This is a thin wrapper for documentation/discoverability.

perf_capture.description: Capture command output into a variable using lastpipe (avoids subshell for the reader). Falls back to $() on older Bash.

perf_benchmark.description: Benchmark a single command with iteration count. Returns JSON with total time, average, and iterations.

pipe_map.description: Apply a function/command to each line echo -e "foo\nbar" | pipe_map upper  # uses MAINFRAME upper()

pipe_filter.description: Filter lines matching a pattern (grep-like) echo -e "1\n2\n3" | pipe_filter '^[12]$'

pipe_reject.description: Filter lines NOT matching a pattern

pipe_take_while.description: Take lines while condition is true

pipe_drop_while.description: Drop lines while condition is true, then emit rest

pipe_unique.description: Remove duplicate lines (preserves order, pure bash)

pipe_field.description: Extract field(s) by position echo "a b c" | pipe_field 1       # outputs: a

pipe_group_count.description: Group and count (like uniq -c but better)

pipe_if.description: Apply different transforms based on condition

pipe_parallel.description: Process lines in parallel (requires GNU parallel or xargs -P)

pipe_peek.description: Tee to stderr (inspect stream without disrupting)

proc.description: Process queries, monitoring, discovery, PID files, locks

proc_memory_percent.description: Get memory as percentage of total

proc_open_files.description: Get count of open file descriptors

pidfile_create.description: Create PID file with current process PID

pidfile_check.description: Check if PID file process is running

proc_wait_timeout.description: Wait for process to exit with timeout

procsub.description: Solve the "variable lost in subshell" problem

read_lines_from.description: Read lines from command output into array without losing variables read_lines_from "ls -1" files echo "Found ${#files[@]} files"

for_each_line.description: Execute callback for each line from command, keeping variables in scope count=0 for_each_line "cat data.txt" 'echo "Line: $line"; ((count++))' echo "Processed $count lines" Notes: - The variable 'line' is available in the callback - All variable changes persist in the current shell

diff_commands.description: Diff two commands' outputs using process substitution diff_commands "sort file1" "sort file2" diff_commands "ls dir1" "ls dir2" -u

capture_output.description: Read command output into variable without subshell capture_output result "date +%Y-%m-%d" echo "Today is: $result"

process_file.description: Process file lines with callback, preserving state in current shell total=0 process_file "data.csv" 'IFS=, read -r name value <<< "$line"; total=$((total + value))' echo "Sum: $total" Notes: - The variable 'line' contains each line - The variable 'lineno' contains current line number (1-based)

tee_to_var.description: Tee command output to variable AND stdout simultaneously tee_to_var output "ls -la" # Output was displayed AND captured in $output echo "Captured ${#output} bytes"

map_lines_from.description: Map function over command output, collecting results in array to_upper() { printf '%s\n' "${1^^}"; } map_lines_from "echo -e 'hello\nworld'" to_upper results echo "${results[@]}"  # HELLO WORLD

filter_lines_from.description: Filter lines from command using predicate function is_even() { [[ $(($1 % 2)) -eq 0 ]]; } filter_lines_from "seq 1 10" is_even evens echo "${evens[@]}"  # 2 4 6 8 10

reduce_lines_from.description: Reduce lines from command to single value sum_reducer() { echo $(($1 + $2)); } reduce_lines_from "seq 1 5" sum_reducer 0 total echo "$total"  # 15

commands_equal.description: Compare two commands for equality if commands_equal "cat file1 | sort" "cat file2 | sort"; then echo "Files have same content" fi

read_n_lines_from.description: Read first N lines from command into array read_n_lines_from "cat largefile.txt" 10 first_lines echo "First 10 lines: ${first_lines[*]}"

batch_lines_from.description: Process lines in batches process_batch() { echo "Processing batch of ${#batch[@]} items" printf '%s\n' "${batch[@]}" } batch_lines_from "seq 1 10" 3 process_batch Notes: - The array 'batch' is available in the callback - The variable 'batch_num' contains current batch number (1-based)

interleave_commands.description: Interleave output from two commands interleave_commands "echo -e 'a\nb'" "echo -e '1\n2'" merged echo "${merged[@]}"  # a 1 b 2
